Hop on your bicycle and set out on a picturesque adventure, as you compete with your friends to enjoy the most unforgettable holiday! Designed for 1-4 players, Postcards is a family friendly game that takes you on a journey across France, filled with inspiring culture, stunning landscapes, and delicious local cuisine. The aim of the game is simple: cycle through the 13 different regions of France, visit as many iconic locations as possible, and share your travels by sending postcards back home. Each postcard you send brings you one step closer to victory, so grab your friends, get pedaling, and let the adventures begin! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Components 2 Gameplay 2.1 During your turn 2.1.1 Taking an Action 2.1.2 Sticking a Stamp 2.1.3 Sending Postcards 2.1.4 Gift Cards 2.1.5 End of Turn Overview During a game of Postcards, you will need to move your bicycle across France, set up camps, and collect postcards to send to your loved ones. Setting up camps will allow you to write down memories that will earn you various bonus effects, while sending postcards will give you points and valuable gifts! Components There are 4 type of cards used in the game: - 52x Postcards - 72x Travel Cards - 25x Gift Cards - 13x Itinerary Cards Each player takes a player board and places the 13 Camp tokens of their color on it. Each player randomly take 1 ltinerary card. The remaining litinerary cards are removed from the game. Each player receives 5 Travel cards from the deck to form their starting hand, and 1 random postcard. Gameplay Each player takes their turn clockwise, until a player triggers the end of the game (sends 4 postcards). The game continues until the last player has played their turn. During your turn You must play 3 Travel cards from your hand. For each card played, you must choose between Taking an Action or Sticking a Stamp . You can play 2 Travel cards of your choice to act as any other Travel card. This counts as 2 Travel cards towards your total of 3 Travel cards played. Taking an Action The action of a Travel card is defined by its symbol. There are 3 types: - Movement Action (Bicycle symbol): Move your Bicycle pawn to a region adjacent to the one you are in. - Postcard Action (Postcard symbol): Take an available postcard. You may discard the 3 next to the deck and draw 3 new ones to replace them before you choose. - Camp Action (Camp symbol): Take the leftmost available Camp token from your player board and place it on an available campsite in the region you are in. If its type matches an available Souvenir space on one of your postcards, you may take a Souvenir token from the supply and place it on that Souvenir space. This immediately grants you a bonus action. Bonus Action icons appear above your cards. Bonus actions must be used before the end of your turn or they are lost. Certain camp tokens have a bonus action or bonus points when you play that camp token. If a player manages to place their Camp tokens on ALL the campsites in a region, they immediately score 1 point per camp token they have placed there. Sticking a Stamp Any Travel card can be used to place a stamp. When sticking a stamp, the symbol on the card is ignored. Place a Stamp token on an available Stamp space, on any of your postcards, that matches the color of the Travel card you played. Sending Postcards In addition to playing your 3 Travel cards, you can send a postcard at any time during your turn if: • all the Stamp spaces on that postcard are filled, And • you are in the region indicated on that postcard. When sending a postcard, return all tokens on it to the supply, then immediately score the points indicated in its bottom-right corner and choose 1 Gift card. community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Very simple game. I played it just once and I think that all the games are almost the same.

[Rating: 3/10] Felt too random. Sure the camps are in set locations, but getting the "better" postcards, both in terms of your targeted numbers but also with regards to the bonus actions on them, felt too random.

[Rating: 4/10] A modern take-and-make, but without even the satisfaction of building something. I guess in theory we were competing for camping spots, but France is big; when someone took a camping spot I might eventually want, I probably didn't even know it yet because I was far away. Bah.  [1 play]

[Rating: 5/10] Being French myself, I was naturally drawn to the design and theme. The cards are gorgeous, but the other components feel overly simple by comparison.  Unfortunately, it’s a miss for me. The elements that were meant to feel distinctly French don’t quite land (some location choices are off and others that should have been there to complete the theme aren't), and overall the game reminds me too much of Parks: very charming, but boring to play.

[Rating: 5/10] On the back of the box it says "In this exciting travel game ....", sadly it misses on the exciting. We found the whole experience to be a bit dull, okay so we only played 2 player so there was not a fight for key camp sites - but that only really comes once you pick up some keyring "gift" cards and by that time the game may well be half over. The overall concept is good but mechanically it was uninteresting.

[Rating: 5/10] In this set collection and order fulfillment game, players are executing actions (moving between regions, placing stamps on postcards/orders, placing tents and possibly gaining extra actions) and completing postcards. First to 4 post cards ends the game, and points from various sources. The player with the most points wins. Another small set collection game that like knarr.

[Rating: 5/10] Contract fulfillment game of you moving around france, sending off postcards which need stamps. Can visit campsites for one-time bonuses.  - I never felt like it made me make difficult or meaningful choices.
